atomic_temp_then_rename.evidence: direct write_text to the final path; no tempfile, no os.replace/rename

checkpointing.evidence: records[] is in-memory; the acquisition receipt is written only after the cohort loop finishes, so a kill loses all bookkeeping and writes no receipt. This matches the observed v5 death: 1 pair on disk, no completion sidecar.

de_facto_completion_marker.evidence: metadata.json is written AFTER both wikitext files, so its presence implies both were written. Nothing reads it as a marker, but it is the natural basis for a resume rule.

deterministic_manifest_traversal.evidence: title_rows sliced by fixed COHORT_SIZE/MAX_COHORTS in manifest order

deterministic_output_path.evidence: page_dir(corpus, row['index'], title) is a pure function of the frozen manifest row

existing_pair_validation.evidence: no re-read or hash check of a pre-existing pair

overwrites_existing_output.evidence: before_path.write_text(...) / after_path.write_text(...) are unconditional; there is no exists() guard anywhere in acquire()

partial_write_detection.evidence: no size, hash or sentinel check on an existing file before use

retry_changes_cohort_composition.caveat: This holds only for a run that starts from an empty corpus. A partial-resume would need to reload metadata.json for skipped pages to evaluate the availability thresholds, which no code path does.
retry_changes_cohort_composition.evidence: BEFORE_CUTOFF/AFTER_CUTOFF pin which revision is fetched per title, and the stop rule depends only on accumulated counts over a deterministic traversal. A clean re-run reproduces the same composition.

skip_semantics.evidence: every eligible title is fetched and rewritten every run

state_after_exception.evidence: no try/finally around the write pair; an exception between before_path and after_path leaves a directory with one file and no metadata.json

forbidden: copying the v5 pair into v6 to save one fetch - that would make the cohort depend on where the crash happened
modifying acquire_w6_v3.py, whose sha256 the frozen manifest pins
restarting into corpus-v5, where the first write would overwrite the existing pair non-atomically
option_b_contract: acquire into a NEW corpus-v6 directory, leaving corpus-v5 untouched
reuse the SAME frozen 6,987-title manifest and the same cutoffs, so cohort composition is unchanged
corpus-v5's single pair is retained as failed-run evidence and is NOT copied into v6
do not select or reorder titles based on what v5 happened to acquire
purpose: P2-13 sibling task W6 section 2A: can the v5 acquisition be resumed without endangering the one materialized pair? Static audit only; no network.
still_required_before_any_network_run: tiny-fixture kill/restart harness proving: existing complete pairs preserved, partial pairs detected, missing-only recovery, manifest order preserved, completion sidecar correctness
why: Option A (verified resume) requires skip-on-exists, integrity validation of existing pairs, and atomic writes. None exist, and adding them changes the frozen acquisition script whose sha256 the title manifest pins - the script self-checks that hash and exits if it moved. So a safe resume cannot be built without breaking the freeze that makes the cohort trustworthy.
